Nihilism is frowned upon by people who have an (often unconscious) bias in their head: the idea that all people are hideous crazed monsters unless they have some kind of strict human-generated ruleset in their life.

The most common argument against nihilism, seen often in this thread, is "people will go crazy and start raping and looting and killing because nothing matters anymore, right?" The underlying idea is that humans are fundamentally evil unless a code of laws- created by philosophers, priests, or lawmakers- is forced upon them. The idea is reinforced by authoritarians and the devout because it gives their beliefs an axiomatic reason to exist- they ARE goodness itself, and without them, all that exists is evil.

Real life isn't quite so cut and dry. We know animals can be empathetic, even ones who have never been influenced by human domestication. There's no reason to think that primitive man did nothing except kill and destroy until The Light of Goodness descended upon them by some miracle. Morality may be emphasized and encouraged by philosophies and religions, but it does not come from them- it is derived from basic human traits, an idea that feels alien and unsettling to many people raised to believe otherwise.

Nihilism does not instantly result in chaos and destruction because humans are not fundamentally chaotic and destructive- those impulses are a part of basic humanity, just like empathy and altruism. It can certainly be used to excuse destruction, just like any philosophy or religion can (and has), but at its core it simply relies on basic human righteousness more than many cultures want to accept.

Nihilism starts with assumptions of intrinsic values, so in that sense it is an incomplete philosophy because it fails to address subjective values, only dismiss them.

It is almost like the argument that aesthetics do not matter because they fall outside scientifically measurable criteria. The inability to scientifically measure aesthetics isn't a paradox or a problem in and of itself, but it is a false dilemma when because, they are, it might be presented as a reason to invalidate their effect because 'muh science', or more so pseudo scientific reasoning. Science as a practice has a well known end point, where the scientific method cannot provide any data or testable hypothesis. Science literally has nothing to say on these subjects, for science they can at best be taken down to an 'ultimate given' and no further. That however does not mean science acts as if they do not exist, or have no consequences.

Nihilism in this sense, instead of recognizing an 'ultimate given' of sorts with intrinsic value judgements, can lead to the same issue with its disregard for subjective value judgements simply because it has no tools to address them.
